title: [Performance][Triton] Bound V2 bincount grids and optimize mask packing
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Thanks to [zihanlin-ai](https://github.com/zihanlin-ai) for [PR #15270](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15270), its implementation and optimization ideas. We agree with its two-pass approach: scatter prompt-presence flags, retain atomic output counts, then pack flags into the existing bitmap.

The original operator and tests were migrated unchanged in `129aa5395` before the following optimizations:

- Flatten both kernels to `min(actual Vector cores, total tiles)` programs, distributing tiles evenly through internal loops.
- Cover [#19958](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19958): 64 requests at 1,048,576 tokens previously launched 65,536 programs; the tested A3 now uses at most 40 per stage.
- Pack four flag bytes through a zero-copy int32 view, reducing the per-word reduction width from 32 to 8.
- Preserve the API, persistent layouts, atomic output counts and 1024-token/128-word tiles.
- Fix the reported Triton-Ascend 3.6 `NameError` by constructing the format constants with `tl.constexpr(value)`; the algorithm, grid and tiles are unchanged by that compatibility fix.

Includes the A2/A3 NPU regressions, a release-note fragment and [operator/test documentation](https://github.com/AuroraEmiya/vllm-ascend/blob/1cfbe3680bc64471973bd4b57126422694f35ba8/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/v2/docs/bincount.md).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Faster initialization of penalty state for the measured long histories, with bounded launches at the 1M-token boundary. Short histories with multiple newly admitted requests can incur more initialization work, as reported below. APIs and persistent layouts are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Performance and earlier Qwen3-8B measurements use operator SHA256 `83b871bc…`. The current constants-only compatibility revision is `f07e939b…`; its compatibility checks and project-nightly results are reported separately.

#### Correctness

- **50 NPU tests passed on A3** through normal repository conftests and framework imports. Coverage includes int32/int64, strides, inactive-row preservation, same-word bits across programs, request-row reuse, bit 31 and exact masks/counts.
- Exact #19958 boundaries: 64 requests with 1,047,552 / 1,048,576 / 1,049,600 tokens, vocabulary 151936 and zero output history.
- The compatibility revision passed **27 standalone cases on each of Triton-Ascend 3.2.2 and 3.6.0**, on A3 with fresh caches and the bypass flag unset.
- The A2/A3 nightly guard is retained. Fresh device-test evidence here is A3; the separate A5 follow-up is linked in the checklist.

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_bincount.py
```

Prompt flags retain overlapping non-atomic byte stores of the same value; output counts use atomic additions. Exact test results do not establish a general backend memory-ordering guarantee.

#### Single-operator performance

Main: `5bd7714b5ef39315cc26867bc67826d42ac0760a`; PR15270: `ef792533de1d4fcd25e458eda701fa105ffafeb4`.

Matched A3 Ascend910_9362, CANN 9.2.0, Torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, Triton-Ascend 3.2.2. These values sum **device-task work including initialization**, rather than model latency. Ordinary cases retain ten calls after three warmups.

| Requests / prompt / output | Main ms | PR15270 ms | This PR ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / 32 / 32 | 0.096 | 0.151 | 0.076 |
| 1 / 4096 / 32 | 1.104 | 0.273 | 0.199 |
| 8 / 4096 / 32 | 9.592 | 1.125 | 0.524 |
| 64 / 4096 / 256 | 83.427 | 7.600 | 3.002 |
| 64 / 1047552 / 0 | 25859.443 | 2866.678 | 245.206 |
| 64 / 1048576 / 0 | coreDim=65536 failure | coreDim=65536 failure | 246.632 |
| 64 / 1049600 / 0 | Not rerun | Not rerun | 251.149 |

Large candidate/PR cases retain three calls after one warmup; serialized main retains two. Failed launches are not timing samples.

Across 37 legal nonempty histories, exact three-way checks passed; this PR reduces device work versus PR15270 on 37/37 and main on 31/37. The six regressions versus main are:

| Requests / prompt / output | Main us | PR15270 us | This PR us | Increase vs main us |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 / 1 / 0 | 193.99 | 977.55 | 373.32 | 179.33 |
| 8 / 8 / 4 | 208.78 | 980.49 | 374.80 | 166.02 |
| 8 / 32 / 32 | 261.99 | 987.71 | 383.39 | 121.40 |
| 64 / 1 / 0 | 490.72 | 6607.16 | 2015.25 | 1524.53 |
| 64 / 8 / 4 | 622.77 | 6612.63 | 2014.21 | 1391.44 |
| 64 / 32 / 32 | 1100.46 | 6626.33 | 2030.82 | 930.36 |

**These are request-initialization regressions; the steady-state decode path is unchanged.** `bincount` runs when penalty-using requests are admitted or resumed. It scans the prompt and any output history already present, builds the prompt bitmap and initializes output counts. “Output” in these tables means that existing history; it is normally zero for a fresh request.

Normal decode incrementally updates counts for newly committed tokens and uses the unchanged `apply_penalties` kernel, without rerunning either `bincount` kernel per token. Vocabulary-sized clearing and packing add fixed initialization work, which can outweigh token-scan savings for short histories. The full legal-shape table is in the linked MD.

#### GPQA accuracy

**Project nightly configuration — current compatibility revision.** Used [Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-A3.yaml](https://github.com/AuroraEmiya/vllm-ascend/blob/1cfbe3680bc64471973bd4b57126422694f35ba8/tests/e2e/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-A3.yaml): MRV2, TP2/DP1, MTP3, FULL_DECODE_ONLY, prefix caching and async scheduling; all 198 questions, official chat-CoT, concurrency 32, max output 32768, temperature 1, `presence_penalty=1.5` / `repetition_penalty=1.0`, with no request seed or thinking override. Other settings follow the linked configuration.

Both sources used the same A3 devices, weights and cached Triton-Ascend 3.6 compatibility image, with CANN 9.2.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. This used the project configuration, not the actual nightly image or A5 hardware. Official AISBench source: `0da56eadb2ac85c31c2540f4f5b69af3ec5717a5`.

| Implementation | Correct /198 in rounds 1,2,3 | Mean accuracy | Sample SD |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 171,168,169 | 85.5219% | 0.7715 percentage points |
| Current compatibility revision (f07) | 171,169,168 | 85.5219% | 0.7715 percentage points |

All six runs passed the original 85.1±5 percentage-point range, with 198 unique successful predictions per run. Equal means do not imply identical responses under temperature 1 without a request-level seed. This presence-only configuration does not consume the prompt repetition bitmap.

#### GSM8K serving performance

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model / runner | Qwen3-8B BF16, MRV2, TP1 on one A3 device |
| Server | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs; max model length 40960, max sequences 32, max batched tokens 4096, memory utilization 0.85; prefix caching disabled |
| Dataset | All 1,319 GSM8K test questions; official `gsm8k_gen_0_shot_cot_str_perf` template |
| Input lengths | Dataset-dependent; benchmark reports 96,693 input tokens per run, averaging 73.31 tokens/request |
| Client | AISBench streaming chat, concurrency 32, `request_rate=0`, 32 warmups |
| Generation | `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `top_k=-1`, `seed=42`, `repetition_penalty=1.03`, `enable_thinking=False` |
| Output | Fixed 128 tokens/request: `max_out_len=128`, `ignore_eos=True` |
| Repeats | Two sequential repeats per source, in main / PR15270 / this PR order, on the same device |

All sources use the same weights, runtime and Python tree except the penalty module. Upstream vLLM is `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`; the common plugin Python base is `c0e0e05b94830034e40270384002d5ba5a416821`. The runtime is CANN 9.2.0, Torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 and Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

This is an **unprofiled serving-performance test**, using GSM8K as the workload rather than reporting a GSM8K accuracy score. Each run completed 1,319 requests, with zero failures and 168,832 generated tokens.

| Implementation | Mean output token/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms | Mean E2EL ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 1448.24 | 156.75 | 20.70 | 2784.70 |
| PR15270 | 1470.24 | 162.50 | 20.30 | 2742.10 |
| This PR | 1467.56 | 169.90 | 20.30 | 2746.00 |

Mean throughput is +1.33% versus main and −0.18% versus PR15270; TTFT is worse in these runs. Two sequential repeats without reverse-order confirmation do not establish a stable whole-model speedup. Full per-run results are in the linked MD.

Captured bincount device-work shares were **0.00836%** for one request generating 64 tokens and **0.03652%** for eight GSM8K requests generating 512 tokens in total. These divide inclusive bincount device-task time by all captured device-task time; they are not end-to-end wall-clock or critical-path shares.

#### Compilation

Changing only grid or tensor contents reuses binaries. Scalar exact-one/divisibility classes, dtype and pointer alignment can create variants; the audited 32-request/40960-context profile has a scoped estimate of at most nine statistics and three packing variants. No startup warmup integration is added.

### Checklist

- [x] **Correctness:** 50 A3 NPU tests, including #19958 boundaries, same-word bits and request-row reuse.
- [x] **Performance:** main/PR15270 comparisons, legal short-history regressions and GSM8K serving results recorded.
- [x] **GPQA project-nightly accuracy:** Qwen3.8-27B main 171/168/169 and current 171/169/168; both mean 85.5219%, all six within 85.1±5pp on the A3 compatibility runtime.
- [x] **A5 compatibility:** [reported working on A5](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20258#issuecomment-6519999362); the constexpr fix also passed the A3 Triton-Ascend 3.6 checks above.
- [x] **Specialization:** scalar/type/alignment classes reviewed; no warmup integration.
- [x] **CI:** required checks passed for unchanged head `1cfbe3680`. [Workflow](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41043089875); A5 was skipped.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
